lines: # IMPORTANT: Update these with your actual domain
SESSION_DOMAIN=null # Keep as null unless required for sharing session cookies with subdomains like SSO
+# TRUST_PROXIES is read by Laravel's TrustProxies middleware. Since the serversideup
+# web server (Caddy) already validates the proxy before the request reaches PHP,
+# trusting all upstream proxies at the application layer is the expected setup here.
+# TRUSTED_PROXY is read by the serversideup FrankenPHP image to decide which proxies
+# the web server trusts for the forwarded client IP. Without it set correctly, logs,
+# geolocation, and rate limiting see the proxy IP instead of the real visitor IP.
+#   cloudflare (default) - trust Cloudflare ranges (CF-Connecting-IP) + Docker networks
+#   sucuri               - trust Sucuri WAF ranges (X-Forwarded-For) + Docker networks
+#   local                - trust only private/Docker network ranges (X-Forwarded-For)
+# All options except "off" already include the Docker internal ranges, so "cloudflare"
+# covers both Cloudflare and an in-Docker reverse proxy (Traefik/Caddy) at the same time.
+# Only trust proxies you control: a trusted proxy lets a client spoof its IP via headers.
+# Defaults to "local" for the in-Docker reverse proxy setup; switch to "cloudflare"
+# if this instance sits behind Cloudflare.
+# Caddy 2.11 caps request headers at 16KiB and returns 431 above that. Raise the
+# limit so large cookies don't break requests, while staying well under the old 1MB.
+      # Code is baked into the image, so cache it until the container restarts
+      # instead of checking the filesystem on every request. Rebuild/restart to
+      # ship new code; do not hot-patch a running container.
+      # Validate Laravel is up, not just that Caddy accepts connections
+      # Boot runs migrations plus the AUTORUN cache builds, so give it room
